title: Group Project (Sessions 2 & 12)

learningObjectives.text: Know the four group project checkpoints and what each one requires
Understand how Prova is used to give feedback on project ideas and to evaluate your final presentation
Know how the 100 project points are earned and how the participation score scales them
Know the showcase attendance expectation and the deadline for reporting a conflict
Be able to choose a project scope and data source that can be completed within the semester

facts: Checkpoint 1: Breaking Bread — meet Wed Sep 9, due Sat Sep 12; eat together, ≥60 minutes, five-minute transformative-experience story; each member submits a short response

Checkpoint 2: Brainstorming and Narrowing — meet Wed Oct 14, due Sat Oct 17; 2-3 page doc: projects that stood out; at least 10 possible businesses with contact, position, relationship; top three ideas (problem, analysis type, data source); one member uploads
Checkpoint 3: Committing to Your Idea — meet Mon Nov 2, due Tue Nov 3; pitch top three ideas to Prova; submit Prova output + one-page proposal (managerial question, analysis type, data needed)
Checkpoint 4: Final Submission — meet Wed Dec 2, due Sat Dec 5; deck, data, analysis, supporting files; every number traceable
Presentations to Prova planned Mon Dec 7 and Wed Dec 9 (Groups 1-6 Monday, 7-12 Wednesday; Section 002 Groups 7-11 Wed); recorded; any member may be asked about any part
Deck structure: company background/history; managerial problem; method, analysis, results (bulk); recommendations and conclusions
Participation Survey opens Wed Dec 9, closes Sat Dec 12

Final Project Showcase planned Mon Dec 14, 11:00 a.m.-2:00 p.m.; top groups by Prova score invited (honor, no extra credit); ALL students expected to attend; conflict must be reported by the Checkpoint 2 due date (Sat Oct 17) to be excused; otherwise forfeit the 2 attendance points

Points: Prova assessment 50; analysis (deck, data, files) evaluated by Prof. Lewis with input from Prova 40; Checkpoints 1-4 on time 8 (2 each); showcase attendance 2; total 100; project = 15% of final grade
Participation Score = Actual % of workload shared ÷ Ideal % (100%/group size; 20% in a group of five); Group Project Grade = Participation Score × Project Score
Tips: choose a setting where tools help a decision-maker; keep scope narrow; focus on the problem, not the tool; act as a consulting team; start early on company data; use personal networks
Prior projects (18) by analysis: Elasticity & Price Discrimination (4), Pricing for Revenue & Profit (7), Production & Cost (6), Competition & Game Theory (1)
